heading_path: Chapter 9: ART for Children & Adolescents > 9.3 Tuberculosis Preventive Therapy (TPT) for Treatment of Latent TB Infection (LTBI) > TPT regimens and dosing
text:
### TPT regimens and dosing by ART regimen, age and weight

| Population | Drug Regimen | Dosing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| All clients on DTG or EFV based ART | Preferred ≥14 yr & 30kg: 3HP + Vit B6 (Once-weekly Isoniazid + Rifampicin x 3mo) | Vit B6 once weekly + 3 adult tabs once weekly of 3HP (300mg INH/300mg Rifapentine) |
| All clients on DTG or EFV based ART | Alternative: 6H | See INH dosing chart |
| All clients on DTG or EFV based ART | Preferred <14 yr or <30kg: 6H + Vit B6 (Once daily Isoniazid + B6 x 6 mo). \*TPT in those <12 months only if there is a new known pulmonary TB contact | \*Vit B6 OD + 6H (100mg INH) dosing by weight: <5kg 0.5 OD; 5-9.9kg 1 OD; 10-13.9kg 1.5 OD; 14-19.9kg 2 OD; 20-24.9kg 2.5 OD; ≥25kg 1 adult tab (300mg) |
| All clients on PI-Based ART | Preferred: 6H | See INH dosing chart |

*See below for Pyridoxine (Vit B6) Dosing.

| Population | Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6) | Special Considerations |
| --- | --- | --- |

heading_path: Chapter 9: ART for Children & Adolescents > 9.4 ART for Children & Adolescents with TB/HIV Coinfection (annex 11.16) > Children initiating TB treatment while on ART
text:
### ART changes for children initiating TB treatment while on ART

**Children initiating TB treatment while on ART**

| Current ART | Changes |
| --- | --- |
| DTG [note 2]-based | Increase DTG [note 2] to twice daily dosing. Continue current backbone. |
| LPV/r [note 3] | Preferred: If DTG-naïve, transition to a DTG [note 2]-based regimen (with appropriate dose adjustment). Continue current backbone. Alternative: If DTG is not possible, LPV/r [note 3] dose adjustment is needed: Ritonavir (RTV) dose needs to be "super-boosted" to achieve the same dose as LPV in mg, in a ratio equal to or approaching 1:1. In older children and adolescents swallowing tablets the LPV/r dose can be doubled. |
| DRV/r | Change of regimen is needed: replace DRV/r with DTG [note 2] if DTG-naive or with LPV/r [note 3] if DTG-experienced (with appropriate dose adjustment). Continue current backbone. |
| ATV/r | Change of regimen is needed: replace ATV/r with DTG if DTG-naive or with LPV/r [note 3] if DTG-experienced (with appropriate dose adjustment). Continue current backbone. |

**Notes (applies to every row in this section):** *Maintain all dose adjustments for 2 weeks after completion of ATT. *The preferred regimen for children with DTG resistance is an optimized NRTI backbone with LPV/r [note 3]. If this is not available a holding regimen of AZT/3TC/ABC OR NNRTI based therapy may be necessary. Please consult with an expert in Paediatric HIV/TB.

**Neonates (first 28 days of life) initiating TB treatment while on ART**

| Current ART | Changes | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NVP [note 1]-based | Change of regimen is needed: substitute NVP as soon as possible with DTG [note 2] or LPV/r [note 3] (with appropriate dose adjustment). |  |

[note 1] Do not use lead in dosing and use the maximum recommended dose by neonatal dosing chart if administering with rifampicin. Transition to DTG when 3 kgs and 4 weeks of age.
[note 2] DTG should be dosed twice daily in children on TB treatment. This dose adjustment must continue for 2 weeks after completing ATT.
[note 3] If used, LPV/r dose adjustment is needed: ritonavir (RTV) dose needs to be "super-boosted" to achieve the same dose as LPV in mg, in a ratio equal to or approaching 1:1. In older children and adolescents swallowing tablets the LPV/r dose can be doubled. This dose adjustment must continue for 2 weeks after completing ATT.

### Second-line ART for children and adolescents by weight and current first-line regimen

| Weight | Current 1st line Regimen | Preferred 2nd Line Regimen | Alternative 2nd Line Regimen |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3 - 29.9 kg | AZT + 3TC + NVP (or EFV) | ABC + 3TC + DTG | - |
| 3 - 29.9 kg | ABC + 3TC + NVP (or EFV) | AZT + 3TC + DTG | - |
| 3 - 29.9 kg | ABC + 3TC + DTG | Refer to National HIVDR Clinical Expert Committee. Only switch to 2nd line if genotype test (resistance test) shows DTG-resistance or PI-resistance. The 2nd line regimen should be determined by the genotype results. | (same as left) |
| 3 - 29.9 kg | AZT + 3TC + DTG | Refer to National HIVDR Clinical Expert Committee. Only switch to 2nd line if genotype test (resistance test) shows DTG-resistance or PI-resistance. The 2nd line regimen should be determined by the genotype results. | (same as left) |
| 3 - 29.9 kg | AZT + 3TC + LPV/r OR ABC + 3TC + LPV/r | Refer to National HIVDR Clinical Expert Committee. Only switch to 2nd line if genotype test (resistance test) shows DTG-resistance or PI-resistance. The 2nd line regimen should be determined by the genotype results. | (same as left) |
| ≥ 30 kg | AZT + 3TC + NVP (or EFV) | TDF + 3TC + DTG | ABC + 3TC + DTG; TDF + 3TC + boosted PI\*\* (ATV/r\* or LPV/r or DRV/r\*\*) |
| ≥ 30 kg | ABC + 3TC + NVP (or EFV) | TDF + 3TC + DTG | AZT + 3TC + DTG; TDF + 3TC + boosted PI\*\* (ATV/r\* or LPV/r or DRV/r\*\*) |
| ≥ 30 kg | TDF + 3TC + EFV | TDF + 3TC + DTG | AZT + 3TC + DTG; TDF + 3TC + boosted PI (ATV/r\* or LPV [text cut off in the source] |
| ≥ 30 kg | TDF + 3TC + DTG; ABC + 3TC + DTG; AZT + 3TC + DTG | Refer to National HIVDR Clinical Expert Committee. Only switch to 2nd line if resistance test shows DTG resistance and the 2nd line regimen should be a boosted PI + 2 NRTIs determined by the genotype results. | (same as left) |

**Special Considerations (applies to every row):** *Concept: When changing to 2nd line, in most cases, it is important to change 2 drugs to maintain a robust regimen. Evidence-based exceptions include TLE to TLD and PI based regimens where the NRTI backbone can be recycled. *LPV/r can be changed to ATV/r once client is ≥40kg regardless of VL. **DRV/r can only be used for second line in cases of confirmed INSTI resistance on genotype. Consult HIVDR clinical expert committee.

**Note:** Children and adolescents with at least 2 consecutive detectable VL results while on DTG- or PI-based regimens should be referred to the National HIVDR Clinical Expert Committee (snapthirdline@mohcoag.com) for evaluation of drug resistance and need for genotyping. HIV genotyping (resistance testing) should be done for all clients failing on a DTG- or PI-based ART regimen. Only switch to 2nd line if the resistance test shows DTG resistance and the 2nd line regimen should be a boosted PI + 2 NRTIs determined by the genotype results.

Refer to Annex 11.19 for the paediatrics dosing chart.
